findings.subject: AtomMessage (iOS)
findings.summary: VoiceOver most likely reads only the sender, time and status of an AtomMessage, not the message text.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/AtomMessage.swift:135-137 applies .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) and then .accessibilityLabel(Text(sender)); an explicit label replaces the combined children's label. No test covers it. Verifier: confirm with the Accessibility Inspector on the catalog's message showcase.
findings.fix: Keep the combined element but put the sender in the label together with the text (e.g. accessibilityLabel(Text("\(sender): ") + text) for the text initializer, or drop the explicit label and prepend a hidden sender Text), and add a test that reads the accessibility label.

verified.reason: AtomMessage.swift:135-137 does what the finding says. The bubble calls .accessibilityElement(children: .combine), then .accessibilityLabel(Text(sender)), then .accessibilityValue(time, status). In SwiftUI an explicit accessibilityLabel on a combined element replaces the label merged from its children, so the content Text is dropped. VoiceOver reads only the sender plus the time and status. AtomMessageTests.swift has no accessibility assertions; it checks only enum labels and an ImageRenderer smoke test. No wrapper or documented decision covers this. Not run in the Accessibility Inspector; this verdict comes from reading the source.

findings.subject: chat-typing-indicator
findings.summary: The typing indicator most likely announces nothing to screen readers in its documented placement.
findings.evidence: chat-typing-indicator.tsx:22-36 is role=status named only by aria-label with all children aria-hidden; live regions announce content, not names. All three documented compositions put it inside an aria-busy ChatMessage (chat-typing-indicator.stories.tsx:22, apps/docs/src/pages/pattern-agent.mdx:67-82, packages/templates/src/blocks/chat-panel/chat-panel.tsx:130-146), which holds back announcements. Verifier: check with VoiceOver/NVDA on the InMessage story.
findings.fix: Render the label as visually hidden text inside the status region (not aria-label), and announce from a region that is not under aria-busy (or drop aria-busy until the first text arrives); add a test for the text content and update the guidance.

verified.reason: The code matches the finding. chat-typing-indicator.tsx is a role=status span with only aria-label, and every child is aria-hidden. ChatMessage sets aria-busy when streaming (chat-message.tsx:69). All three compositions render the indicator inside a streaming ChatMessage: the InMessage story, pattern-agent.mdx:82 and chat-panel.tsx:146. The live region is also inserted together with its name rather than updated, so 'announces it once' in the component's comment is unlikely to hold. It is real, but it is lower than P1. The indicator is a transient extra, and the reply text and the message itself still reach assistive technology once streaming ends. Losing the typing cue does not make the chat unusable or block it from being ready. Not checked with a screen reader.
